conclusion: Multiple has a verified question-final existential and definite partitives. Countless has relative-modified existentials and partitives, including an academic partitive in 2008. The cline follow-up also confirms independent numerous and relative-modified existentials with numerous and certain. A possible ordering by decreasing overt nominal support remains a hypothesis; partitives and relatives may be parallel rather than consecutive stages. No frequency, historical-order, broad acceptability, or maintenance claim is established. Isolated unmodified There are countless/numerous/various/certain remains outside the demonstrated findings.

cgel_cline_checks.pp411-414: Distinguishes explicit/implicit partitive, simple anaphoric, and special-interpretation independent uses.
cgel_cline_checks.p413: Certain and various strongly resist omission of the partitive of phrase. These restrictions differ from either/neither/which/both, whose of phrase can be absent under the appropriate interpretation.
cgel_cline_checks.p413_limits: Genitives exclude these direct partitives; demonstrative those has restricted partitive use requiring a following modifier. A universal scale from partitives to independent use is therefore unsuitable for the entire Noun/Determinative inventory.
cgel_cline_checks.p414: Human special interpretations occur for a restricted list including few/many/all/some; those requires a clausal modifier in this use. Conventional human readings must be distinguished from contextual anaphora.
